newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission to release economic forecasts.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission to release economic forecasts.

text.p: The European Commission will issue economic figures later on Wednesday expected to paint a rosy picture of the European Union's march to a single currency.

Forecasts to be released at noon (1100 GMT) will give the EU executive's view of how each of the bloc's 15 countries will perform in 1997, the year on which they will be tested for their fitness to join in a single currency on January 1, 1999.
Markets are expected to treat the forecasts -- particularly the key figure on the public deficit to Gross Domestic Product ratio -- with some degree of scepticsm.
The Commission is widely expected to show many countries, including France and Germany, meeting the three percent deficit to GDP requirement.
Economists have said the Commission, as an advocate of the single currency, is under strong pressure to put the best light on the picture.
Anything more that three percent for France and Germany likely would cause a sharp market reaction as it would indicate the situation was more difficult than expected, some economists have said.
